test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 4 Mar 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: What is the minimum amount of monthly pension permissible under Atal Pension Yojana?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rs**__ __**1,000.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Atal Pension Yojana was launched in** 2015 **by the **Government of India** to provide a guaranteed pension to workers in the unorganized sector.
 
• The scheme is open to all Indian citizens aged **18** to **40** years who have a savings account in a bank or post office.
 
• Subscribers can receive a fixed monthly pension ranging from Rs. **1,000** to Rs. **5,000**, depending on their contribution and age at entry.
 
• **Government Co-contribution:** For eligible subscribers, the government co-contributes 50% of the total contribution or Rs. 1,000 annually, whichever is lower, for a period of 5 years (2015-2020).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-Dhan (PM-SYM)**

 
 
• It was launched in **2019**, the scheme aims to provide a monthly pension of Rs. 3,000 to unorganized sector workers after the age of 60.
 
• It is targeted at workers in the **unorganized sector** aged 18 to 40 years with a monthly income of up to Rs. 15,000, requiring contributions ranging from Rs. 55 to Rs. 200 per month, depending on the age at entry.
 
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY)**
 
 
• It was launched in **2014**, PMJDY aims at ensuring access to financial services, including bank accounts, credit, insurance, and pensions, especially for the underprivileged sections of society.
 
• Under PMJDY, people can open **zero-balance** savings accounts with no minimum balance requirement, and they also get benefits like a RuPay debit card and accidental insurance coverage.
 
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY):**
 
 
• It was launched in 2016, **PMFBY** aims to provide affordable crop insurance to farmers against natural calamities, pests, and diseases to ensure financial security and risk mitigation.
 
• The scheme offers low premium rates: 2% for Kharif crops, 1.5% for Rabi crops, and 5% for **commercial** and **horticultural** crops, with the rest of the premium subsidized by the government.
